column.text: Crypto just absorbed more than $1,000,000,000 in liquidations across a 10-minute span, as BTC broke below $74,000, ETH slipped under $2,125, XRP under $1.10 and SOL under $90. The crowd was leaning long into a market that was already losing its bid, and the forced unwind shows how crowded that positioning was. Flows confirm the damage. Friday's BTC ETF outflows came in at −$411.9M, pushing the 7-day net to −$1908.0M. ETH posted −$93.2M on Friday and −$626.6M over seven days. SOL shed −$25.1M on Friday, −$64.7M over the week. Institutions are not buying this dip. Momentum is the trade. The regime is RISK_OFF, the tape is down-trending, and dollar liquidity is contracting, so failed rallies are the better-odds shorts and continuation shorts carry the tailwind. BTC's daily RSI at 35.74 and ETH's at 34.46 look stretched, and Fear & Greed reads 29, but oversold is not a mechanism. On a falling tape, it is how traders get early and then get stopped out. Longs need a real reason: deeply negative funding, a capitulation print, a failed breakdown that reclaims levels, or a demand catalyst. Without one, the $73k BTC support is a line to watch for a clean break, not a floor to buy. US jobs data is the macro catalyst most likely to test it, and equity-correlated crypto will feel that first. Size shorts to momentum, respect squeezes around liquidation clusters, and wait for proof before chasing any reclaim. Watch whether $73k holds into the jobs print, because a clean loss opens the next leg lower.
